title: A tuberculosis vaccine that interrupts transmission

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a tuberculosis vaccine that provides reliable, durable protection in people with and without prior Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, including relevant high-risk groups, and demonstrably reduces transmission in communities. Its intended benefit extends from protecting vaccinated individuals against pulmonary disease to reducing the spread of infection. The supplied evidence establishes a narrower vaccine benefit in one population, rather than achievement of this broader goal.

Conceptual distinction: preventing acquisition of infection, preventing progression from existing infection to pulmonary disease, and reducing onward transmission are different outcomes. A vaccine could contribute to transmission reduction by preventing infectious disease, even without preventing every infection. Conversely, fewer infections or disease cases among vaccine recipients would not by itself establish the size or durability of the community transmission effect.

significance.text: Durable protection across populations could shift tuberculosis control toward sustained prevention. The M72/AS01E trial provides an experimental basis for that possibility by showing that vaccination can reduce progression to pulmonary disease in previously infected adults. Extending protection to uninfected people and a wider range of ages and risk groups, while demonstrating reduced transmission, would substantially broaden the public-health value beyond the result established in that trial.

Conditional impact synthesis: if vaccination substantially reduced infectious pulmonary disease and onward spread, it could protect both recipients and people whose exposure falls as community transmission declines. Those indirect benefits would depend on the magnitude and duration of protection, vaccination coverage, and delivery in settings where transmission occurs. Elimination would still require management of existing infection and disease; individual vaccine efficacy alone does not establish elimination. The supplied material offers no historical comparison against which to calibrate the scale of the potential advance.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central capability still to be demonstrated within the supplied evidence is durable vaccine protection across infection histories and relevant populations, coupled to a measured reduction in transmission. The 2019 study supports protection against progression to pulmonary disease in infected, HIV-negative adults, but does not establish protection in uninfected people or across broader age and risk groups. Its discussion calls for confirmation in larger, longer studies and more diverse populations. Whether subsequent work has achieved any of these broader capabilities is not established by the supplied record.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: the development challenge is to induce protection that remains effective over time, works despite differences in prior infection and host risk, and can be delivered safely at sufficient scale. The measurement challenge is to distinguish protection against disease progression from protection against infection and from reduced onward spread. Demonstrating the last of these requires population evidence beyond the individual pulmonary-disease endpoint used in the supplied trial.

Biological uncertainty: the earlier research framed the difficulty partly in terms of years-long bacterial persistence and evasion of or resistance to immune responses. The supplied review did not identify direct support for those specific mechanistic assertions in the retained evidence. They remain possible explanatory context requiring additional evidence, rather than established mechanisms on which this record relies.

current_state.text: Tait and colleagues’ final analysis of the phase 2b M72/AS01E trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine on 29 October 2019, demonstrated protection against progression to bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis in Mycobacterium tuberculosis-infected, HIV-negative adults aged 18–50 years. Estimated vaccine efficacy at month 36 was 49.7%, with a 95% confidence interval of 2.1–74.2%. The wide interval leaves substantial uncertainty about the magnitude of protection, while preserving the trial’s demonstrated evidence of benefit in its studied population.

The trial’s endpoint concerned pulmonary disease. It did not establish prevention of infection acquisition, interruption of transmission, protection in uninfected people, or efficacy across the full range of relevant ages and high-risk groups. The month-36 result also does not establish protection beyond the observed follow-up. Broader population protection and transmission reduction remain extensions to be demonstrated, rather than outcomes that can be inferred directly from the reported efficacy estimate.

Evidence boundary: the supplied review reports verification of the complete main article, including pages 1–12 and references, without extraction truncation; separately referenced supplements were not supplied. The trial findings summarized here are therefore based on that review of the main article. The record contains no subsequent-development assessment establishing the field’s status through 1 November 2026 or the source-retrieval date of 11 November 2026. This limits claims about present-day progress without undermining the dated 2019 result.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: large, long-term trials in multiple high-incidence settings should show strong protection against pulmonary tuberculosis, with acceptable safety in prespecified populations that include people with and without prior infection and relevant age and risk groups. The trial paper’s call for larger, longer studies across infection status, geography, ethnicity, and age supports this expansion beyond its original population. The meaning of strong protection, the required duration, and the relevant safety boundaries should be specified prospectively; these are proposed criteria rather than established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Durable pulmonary tuberculosis protection across prespecified populations with acceptable safety

completion_criteria.text: Proposed transmission demonstration: community studies should measure a substantial reduction in transmission using prospectively defined endpoints and methods that distinguish the vaccination effect from other changes in tuberculosis control. Infection acquisition should be assessed where appropriate, but reduced acquisition among vaccinated individuals alone would not complete the transmission claim. Evidence should connect individual protection to a measurable population effect and establish how that effect depends on coverage and time since vaccination.
completion_criteria.label: Community transmission reduction attributable to vaccination across coverage and time

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: convincing evidence would include confirmation across independent studies or populations, transparent outcome definitions and analyses, and sufficient follow-up to characterize waning protection. Practical evaluation should establish whether the vaccine can reach intended populations under feasible delivery conditions while maintaining acceptable safety and benefit. Successful finite studies would demonstrate breadth within the populations, settings, and durations tested; they would not establish literal universality or guarantee elimination.
completion_criteria.label: Reproducible protection with characterized waning and feasible delivery boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: INF-12, “Very short, reliable curative treatment for active and latent tuberculosis,” is the closest complement. Both could reduce future tuberculosis burden, including disease arising from existing infection. INF-03 seeks immune protection through vaccination, whereas INF-12 seeks curative treatment of active or latent infection. Vaccinating previously infected people overlaps with preventing disease progression, but the supplied vaccine trial does not establish eradication of infection. The supplied roster supports this distinction even though the reviewed trial itself does not characterize INF-12.

Roster-based comparison: INF-01, “A broadly protective HIV vaccine,” INF-08, “A pre-emptive vaccine against diverse pandemic coronaviruses,” and INF-13, “A highly protective, durable and readily deliverable malaria vaccine,” share the ambition of broad preventive protection. Each retains a distinct pathogen, target population, and biological challenge. INF-09, “A rapid, end-to-end vaccine response to a newly identified pathogen,” instead centers on development and deployment speed; INF-03 centers on durable tuberculosis protection and demonstrated transmission reduction.

Roster-based comparison: INF-04, “A reliable way to break malaria transmission through its vectors,” shares the population-level objective of reducing spread, but intervenes through vectors rather than tuberculosis vaccination. INF-10, “Prevention of multiple sclerosis by controlling Epstein–Barr virus,” and INF-14, “Mechanism-guided prevention of major post-viral syndromes,” concern prevention of downstream illness associated with infection. INF-03 specifically targets tuberculosis infection, pulmonary disease, and transmission, with each outcome requiring separate evidence.

Roster-based comparison: INF-02, “A safe, scalable cure for established HIV infection,” and INF-11, “A safe, broadly effective treatment-free cure for chronic hepatitis B,” concern cures for established infections rather than vaccine protection. INF-05, “Near-patient diagnosis of the cause and treatability of most serious infections,” could support disease identification and management. INF-06, “A dependable platform for generating new antibacterial treatments,” INF-07, “Broad-spectrum treatment for unrelated viral infections,” and INF-15, “A rapidly adaptable clinical phage-therapy platform,” concern therapeutic capabilities. These entries remain distinct from INF-03, while illustrating complementary routes to controlling infectious disease.

change_log.change: Preserved INF-03 and its title while explaining the distinction between infection prevention, prevention of pulmonary disease, and transmission reduction.
change_log.reason: These outcomes are related but cannot substitute for one another when evaluating the proposed innovation.

change_log.change: Expanded the M72/AS01E result to include the 2019 publication date, phase 2b design, infected and HIV-negative population aged 18–50, bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary-disease endpoint, month-36 efficacy of 49.7%, and 95% confidence interval of 2.1–74.2%.
change_log.reason: The review supports these details, which define the demonstrated benefit and its uncertainty.

change_log.change: Qualified bacterial persistence and immune-evasion assertions instead of presenting them as established mechanisms or deleting the concept.
change_log.reason: The supplied review did not find direct support for those assertions in the retained evidence.

change_log.change: Separated the historical trial result from the unresolved status of subsequent developments through November 2026.
change_log.reason: A valid 2019 result does not establish the field’s present-day state, and missing freshness evidence does not invalidate that result.

change_log.change: Made community transmission measurement explicit in the proposed completion criteria and added prospective thresholds, reproducibility, and practical boundaries.
change_log.reason: Reduced infection in recipients alone does not establish reduced onward transmission; proposed benchmarks must remain distinct from published standards.

change_log.change: Integrated conditional population benefits and implementation limits without implying elimination follows from vaccine efficacy.
change_log.reason: Coverage, delivery, durability, and management of existing disease remain relevant to the potential impact.

change_log.change: Retained and refined the distinction from INF-12 using its supplied roster title, and explained relevant relationships across the roster.
change_log.reason: The roster explicitly identifies INF-12 as treatment for active and latent tuberculosis, resolving the narrow characterization gap identified in the review without supplying evidence about its technical progress.

change_log.change: Preserved the main-article and supplement access boundaries.
change_log.reason: The supplied review covered the complete main article, while separately referenced supplements were unavailable.

unresolved_issues: Subsequent vaccine developments and whether the broader goal remains unmet through November 2026 are not established by the supplied evidence.
The supplied evidence does not directly substantiate the earlier claims about years-long bacterial persistence or specific immune-evasion mechanisms.

The magnitude and durability of protection outside the studied infected, HIV-negative adult population, and any effect on infection acquisition or community transmission, are not established by this trial.
Numerical efficacy and transmission thresholds, follow-up duration, intended population coverage, and acceptable safety boundaries remain proposed design choices requiring prospective definition.
Separately referenced trial supplements were not supplied, so conclusions dependent on their contents cannot be assessed here.

The review’s recommendation to remove the characterization of INF-12 was not adopted in full because the supplied roster explicitly identifies its focus on curative treatment of active and latent tuberculosis. That title supports the conceptual distinction but does not establish INF-12’s evidence or development status.

brief.title: A tuberculosis vaccine that also reduces its spread
possible: People could get lasting protection against tuberculosis whether or not they already carry the bacterium. That protection would extend across ages and include people at higher risk.
why: Reducing infectious lung disease and its spread could protect both vaccinated people and others whose exposure falls. Tuberculosis control could shift toward sustained prevention.

sources.showed: The candidate vaccine M72/AS01E reduced progression to lung tuberculosis in adults who already carried the bacterium and did not have HIV.
sources.quote:
Among adults infected with M. tuberculosis, vaccination with M72/AS01E elicited an im-
mune response and provided protection against progression to pulmonary tuberculosis 
disease for at least 3 years.
sources.cited_for: Vaccination can prevent lung disease in people already infected with the tuberculosis bacterium.
sources.not_established: The trial did not establish protection in uninfected people or reduced community transmission.

sources.showed: Among household contacts of people with tuberculosis in India, neither tested vaccine showed overall protection against lung disease. VPM1002 protected against tuberculosis outside the lungs.
sources.quote: Both vaccines were well tolerated with mild local reactions in about a third of participants.
sources.cited_for: A broader trial found acceptable tolerability but did not demonstrate the lung protection needed for this goal.
sources.not_established: Protection against disease outside the lungs does not establish prevention of infectious lung disease or community spread.

sources.who: Paulo Cesar Pereira dos Santos and colleagues
sources.showed: BCG-Denmark, a version of the existing tuberculosis vaccine, did not reduce new positive results on QFT Plus, a blood test used as a sign of infection, in Brazilian health workers.
sources.quote: BCG-Denmark vaccination did not reduce initial QFT Plus conversion risk in Brazilian health-care workers.
sources.cited_for: Trials of the existing vaccine have not consistently shown protection against signs of new infection.
sources.not_established: Blood-test results alone cannot establish whether vaccination reduces community transmission.

shown: Tait and colleagues found that M72/AS01E roughly halved the risk of lung tuberculosis in already infected adults without HIV. The size of that benefit remained uncertain.

Other trials show the difficulty of extending protection. Singh and colleagues found no overall protection against lung tuberculosis with either vaccine tested. Pereira dos Santos and colleagues found no protection against blood-test signs of new infection.
missing: Lasting, safe protection against lung tuberculosis across infection histories, ages and relevant high-risk groups remains to be demonstrated.
Community studies must establish how much vaccination reduces transmission and how that effect depends on coverage and time.
Independent confirmation must establish how protection fades and whether feasible delivery preserves safety and benefit.

milestones.label: Lasting, safe lung protection across intended populations
milestones.explanation: Large, long-term trials in several settings with frequent tuberculosis would have to show safe protection across infection histories, ages and risk groups. This would establish breadth beyond the adults already studied.

milestones.label: Less community spread attributable to vaccination
milestones.explanation: Community studies would have to show reduced transmission attributable to vaccination across coverage levels and time. This would connect individual protection to reduced spread.

milestones.label: Repeatable protection with workable delivery and measured fading
milestones.explanation: Independent studies would have to confirm protection, measure how it fades and establish feasible delivery with acceptable safety and benefit. This would define where and for how long vaccination works.

uncertain: How much protection, for how long, should count as success, and what safety limits should apply?
Could preventing infectious lung disease reduce spread substantially even if vaccination does not prevent infection?
How much of a community benefit would depend on the proportion of people vaccinated?

page.title: Tuberculosis vaccines that reduce community transmission
page.definition: A vaccine for adolescents and adults with or without prior Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection prevents pulmonary tuberculosis, the lung form of TB, and reduces transmission to unvaccinated community members.

goal.need: WHO attributes 90% of TB disease to adolescents and adults, the main sources of spread. BCG vaccines have limited protection in these age groups. Preventing pulmonary disease targets illness in recipients and the sources of exposure for other people.

figures.caption: Estimated worldwide tuberculosis burden in 2025
figures.note: Deaths include people living with HIV.

statements.quote: a vaccine to be administered to adolescents and adults for prevention of pulmonary tuberculosis and reduction of transmission
statements.context: WHO identifies this as a priority for new tuberculosis vaccines.

statements.quote: vaccines for all forms of tuberculosis for people of all ages
statements.context: Paragraph 68 includes these vaccines among the objectives of tuberculosis research and innovation funding.

completion.title: TB vaccination reduces new infections among unvaccinated community members.
completion.criterion: In a registered cluster-randomized study of adolescent/adult TB vaccination, initially infection-test-negative, unvaccinated residents have fewer sustained infection-test conversions than residents of control communities. Indirect efficacy, defined as 1 minus the incidence-rate ratio, has a cluster-adjusted two-sided 95% confidence interval wholly above 0%. The registered endpoint specifies the assay, conversion and persistence rules, and follow-up. Infection-test conversion is a proxy for new M. tuberculosis infection.
completion.set_by: Atlas; operational test of community transmission reduction.
completion.basis: Searched WHO's 2018 preferred characteristics, its 2024 evidence considerations and ClinicalTrials.gov for a community-transmission success threshold; none was found. WHO's disease-efficacy targets do not establish indirect protection. Nelson and colleagues describe community randomization for indirect effects. The 95% confidence-interval rule is an Atlas operational choice.

milestones.title: A TB vaccine induces immunity and protection in at least one animal model.
milestones.criterion: A candidate demonstrates both immunogenicity, meaning a vaccine-induced immune response, and protection in at least one animal model, with evidence published in a peer-reviewed journal. This is the Working Group's animal proof-of-concept gate; it does not establish protection in humans.
milestones.set_by: Stop TB Partnership Working Group on New TB Vaccines, preclinical pipeline inclusion criteria.
milestones.threshold_quote: protection and immunogenicity in at least one animal model

milestones.title: A TB vaccine completes phase 1 with immune responses and no safety barrier to phase 2.
milestones.criterion: Completed phase 1a and phase 1b studies support progression: no safety concern precludes further development, and safe dose levels elicit vaccine-specific immune responses sufficient to proceed to phase 2a. For adolescent/adult vaccines, the pathway requires safety data in adults with and without blood-test evidence of prior infection. It specifies no common numerical immune-response cutoff.
milestones.set_by: TuBerculosis Vaccine Initiative, TB Vaccine Development Pathway, Gate E.
milestones.threshold_quote: No safety concerns precluding further clinical development should have been identified.

milestones.title: A TB vaccine meets its predefined phase 2b protective-efficacy criterion.
milestones.criterion: Phase 2b data meet the candidate's predefined minimum protective-efficacy criterion against its primary clinical case definition. The M72/AS01E analysis published on 29 October 2019 found 49.7% efficacy (95% CI 2.1–74.2%) over 3 years in infected, HIV-negative adults aged 18–50 years: 13/1626 cases versus 26/1663. Infection prevention is separate: Brazilian BCG recipients had no reduction in 12-month infection-test conversion (1985 participants; risk ratio 1.09, 95% CI 0.67–1.77), published on 26 February 2024.
milestones.set_by: TuBerculosis Vaccine Initiative, TB Vaccine Development Pathway, Gate G; the minimum is candidate-specific.
milestones.threshold_quote: Evidence of efficacy from Phase 2b or interim analysis consistent with minimal (predefined) TPP criteria

milestones.title: A TB vaccine enters a funded, registered phase 3 trial with regulatory and ethics approvals.
milestones.criterion: A phase 3 TB-vaccine study has committed funding, applicable regulatory and ethics approvals, registration in a recognized trial database, and has begun dosing participants. On 19 March 2024, Gates MRI announced first dosing in the M72/AS01E phase 3 study in South Africa; this sponsor announcement was not peer reviewed. WHO listed M72/AS01E, MTBVAC and GamTBvac in phase 3 in August 2026.
milestones.set_by: Stop TB Partnership Working Group on New TB Vaccines, clinical pipeline advancement criteria.
milestones.threshold_quote: regulatory authority and ethics committee approvals

milestones.title: A pivotal TB-vaccine study shows at least 50% pulmonary-disease efficacy with two years of protection.
milestones.criterion: A randomized, placebo-controlled pivotal study in high-burden countries estimates at least 50% efficacy against microbiologically confirmed pulmonary TB, with at least 2 years of protection. Supportive safety and immunogenicity data include uninfected adults and people living with HIV. These are WHO policy preferences, not a universal licensing floor. PreVenTB, published on 9 April 2026, enrolled 12,717 household contacts aged ≥6 years and followed them for 38 months; neither vaccine established overall pulmonary-TB protection. VPM1002 efficacy was 19.5% (95% CI −14.6% to 43.4%).
milestones.set_by: World Health Organization, 2024 evidence considerations, initial-policy parameters T1.2, T1.4, T1.5 and T1.8.
milestones.threshold_quote: 50% or greater efficacy in preventing confirmed pulmonary TB disease

milestones.title: A new TB vaccine is licensed in at least one country for adolescent/adult pulmonary TB prevention.
milestones.criterion: At least one country's medicines regulator grants a marketing licence for a new vaccine to prevent pulmonary TB in adolescents and adults. The authorized populations and indication must be stated in the licence.
milestones.set_by: Stop TB Partnership Working Group on New TB Vaccines, licensed-vaccine category; applied to the adolescent/adult pulmonary-TB indication.
milestones.threshold_quote: licensed for TB in at least one country

not_found: No registered TB-vaccine community-transmission trial with a numerical success rule was located.
The M72/AS01E phase 3 ClinicalTrials.gov page did not expose its study-record text.

results.finding: M72/AS01E: 49.7% pulmonary-TB efficacy among 3,289 participants at month 36.
results.detail: The phase 2b analysis included previously infected, HIV-negative adults; 13 of 1,626 vaccine recipients and 26 of 1,663 placebo recipients met the primary case definition.
results.quote: The vaccine efficacy at month 36 was 49.7%

results.finding: M72/AS01E: 49.7% pulmonary-TB efficacy among 3,289 participants at month 36.
results.detail: This was a phase 2b trial, and the primary efficacy estimate was below 50%. Participants had evidence of prior infection and were HIV-negative at enrollment; the required supportive data in uninfected adults and people living with HIV were not established here.
results.quote: The vaccine efficacy at month 36 was 49.7%

results.finding: PreVenTB dosed 12,717 participants in a phase 3 trial of VPM1002 and Immuvac.
results.detail: The trial was funded by the Indian Council of Medical Research, registered in the Clinical Trials Registry India, and received regulatory and institutional ethics approvals.
results.quote:
The first participant was enrolled
and vaccinated on 15 July 2019 and the last participant
on 31 December 2020.

results.finding: VPM1002 showed 19.5% pulmonary-TB efficacy in a per-protocol comparison of 7,705 participants.
results.detail: The randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial followed participants for 38 months, but the overall pulmonary efficacy estimate fell below 50% and its 95% CI included zero. The trial excluded participants with HIV.
results.quote:
In the per protocol analysis, VPM1002 
showed vaccine efficacy of 21.4% (95% confidence 
interval (CI) −8.9% to 43.2%), 19.5% (−14.6% to 
43.4%), and 50.4% (0.8% to 75.2%) against all TB, 
pulmonary TB, and extrapulmonary TB, respectively.

results.finding: BCG-Denmark in 1,985 Brazilian adult health-care workers: 12-month infection-test conversion risk ratio was 1.09.
results.detail: The trial found no reduction in initial infection-test conversion. It measured an infection proxy, not protective efficacy against the primary clinical disease definition in a phase 2b trial.
results.quote:
Specifically, 34 (3·4%) of 
996 participants had initial QFT conversion in the BCG group compared with 32 (3·2%) of 989 in the placebo group 
(risk ratio 1·09 [95% CI 0·67–1·77]; p=0·791).

results.finding: BCG-TetOFF-DL induced immune responses and sterilizing protection in 6 of 8 vaccinated macaques.
results.detail: Vaccinated macaques showed sustained airway T-cell responses and significantly lower thoracic bacterial burden than unvaccinated controls. This animal study does not establish protection in humans.
results.quote: Sterilizing immunity occurred in 6 of 8 macaques compared with 2 of 8 wild-type BCG-immunized macaques.

results.finding: MTBVAC induced immune responses in 8 rhesus macaques and reduced lung pathology versus 8 unvaccinated controls (P = 0.003).
results.detail: Before challenge, vaccinated macaques showed increased mycobacterium-specific IFN-γ responses. After challenge, MTBVAC recipients had lower lung pathology scores than unvaccinated controls. P values were unadjusted for multiple comparisons.
results.quote:
Pulmonary disease burden measured by the manual counting
of both discrete and coalesced lesions from serial sections
revealed signiﬁcantly fewer macroscopic lesions in the lungs from
the MTBVAC-vaccinated group compared to either the BCG-
vaccinated group ( P = 0.04) or the unvaccinated group ( P = 0.025)

results.finding: MTBVAC phase 1 enrolled 36 adults; no serious adverse events were reported, and immune responses were at least comparable to BCG.
results.detail: The study reports safety and immune responses in tuberculosis-negative adults, but does not establish completed phase 1a and 1b studies or safety in adults with evidence of prior infection.
results.quote: The safety of vaccination with MTBVAC at all doses was similar to that of BCG, and vaccination did not induce any serious adverse events.

results.finding: MTBVAC in 143 vaccinated adults: 0 vaccine-related serious adverse events; all doses elicited immune responses.
results.detail: The completed phase 1b–2a trial included adults with and without prior TB sensitisation and supports further efficacy evaluation. The text describes earlier adult trials but does not identify or establish completion of a phase 1a study.
results.quote:
No vaccine-related SAEs were reported. All doses of MTBVAC were immunogenic; 
vaccine-induced antigen-specific CD4 T-cell responses peaked 28 days after vaccination.

results.finding: The phase 3 M72/AS01E TB vaccine trial reached full enrollment, with approximately 20,000 participants.
results.detail: The announcement reports an active phase 3 trial and partner support, but does not state that participants have been dosed or that funding, registration, and regulatory and ethics approvals are in place.
results.quote: We’re glad to announce that the Phase 3 clinical trial of the M72/AS01E tuberculosis (TB) vaccine candidate has reached full enrollment eleven months ahead of schedule– with approximately 20,000 participants enrolled.

results.finding: Mycobacterium vaccae vaccine: among 9,428 participants in the efficacy analysis, efficacy against microbiologically confirmed TB was 49.9%.
results.detail: The randomized, placebo-controlled phase III study enrolled people with latent TB infection and assessed outcomes through 30 months. The point estimate falls below 50% (95% CI −17.0% to 78.6%). The text does not report supportive safety and immunogenicity data for uninfected adults or people living with HIV.

results.finding: China approved Mycobacterium vaccae for pulmonary TB prevention in people aged 15–65 with latent infection; sample size not applicable.
results.detail: The regulator classified the product as a therapeutic product and approved a new indication for an already marketed product, rather than licensing it as a new preventive vaccine.
